title: Arrays in Assembly
description:
## Arrays
Arrays in assembly are just consecutive bytes in memory. You access elements using a base address + offset.

```asm
section .data
    nums dd 10, 20, 30, 40, 50   ; array of 5 dwords (4 bytes each)
```

### Accessing elements:
```asm
mov eax, [nums]           ; first element (10)
mov eax, [nums + 4]       ; second element (20)
mov eax, [nums + 8]       ; third element (30)
```

Each `dd` (dword) is 4 bytes, so element `i` is at `[nums + i*4]`.

### Using a register as index:
```asm
mov rcx, 2                     ; index
mov eax, [nums + rcx*4]        ; third element (30)
```

This is where `lea` shines:
```asm
lea rsi, [nums + rcx*4]        ; address of element
mov eax, [rsi]                 ; value at that address
```


---
## Assignment:
LHINX stores boot priorities in an array. Write a function `sum_array` that takes the address of an array in `rdi` and the count in `rsi`, and returns the sum of all elements in `rax`.
setupCode:
section .data
    pass_msg db "PASS", 10
    pass_len equ $ - pass_msg
    fail_msg db "FAIL", 10
    fail_len equ $ - fail_msg
    arr1 dd 10, 20, 30, 40, 50
    arr2 dd 5, 5, 5
    arr3 dd 100

section .text
    global _start
starterCode:
sum_array:
    ; rdi = array address, rsi = count
    ; return sum in rax
    ret
runHarness:
_start:
    lea rdi, [arr1]
    mov rsi, 5
    call sum_array
    cmp rax, 150
    jne .fail
    lea rdi, [arr2]
    mov rsi, 3
    call sum_array
    cmp rax, 15
    jne .fail
    lea rdi, [arr3]
    mov rsi, 1
    call sum_array
    cmp rax, 100
    jne .fail
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, pass_msg
    mov rdx, pass_len
    syscall
    jmp .exit
.fail:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, fail_msg
    mov rdx, fail_len
    syscall
.exit:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hint: Use a loop with rcx as your index. Access each element with [rdi + rcx*4]. Remember dd is 4 bytes. Use eax for the running total since dd elements are 32-bit.
